title: George Mason Ends UConn's Final Four Dream
dek: Denham Brown's buzzer-beating reverse forced overtime, but 11th-seeded George Mason never trailed in the extra period and stunned top-seeded UConn, 86-84, to reach the Final Four.

facts.event: NCAA tournament Washington, D.C. Regional final (Elite Eight)

setup.text: UConn arrived at the regional final as the No. 1 seed in the Washington, D.C. Region, 30-3 and ranked No. 2 in the AP poll. Jim Calhoun's Huskies had beaten Albany, Kentucky and Washington to get there — the last one in overtime on Friday night.

None of those wins came easily. UConn trailed Albany by 12 with 12 minutes left, survived Kentucky by making six free throws in the final 30 seconds, and forced overtime against Washington on Rashad Anderson's long 3-pointer with 1.8 seconds to go.

The roster was stacked with pros-in-waiting. Three months later, Rudy Gay (No. 8), Hilton Armstrong (No. 12), Marcus Williams (No. 22) and Josh Boone (No. 23) went in the first round of the NBA draft and Denham Brown went 40th — making UConn the first school to have five players taken in a two-round draft.

George Mason, a commuter school from Fairfax, Va., in the Colonial Athletic Association, had been a contested at-large pick — CBS commentator Billy Packer was among the critics. The Patriots had never won an NCAA tournament game before this March, then beat Michigan State, North Carolina and Wichita State. The Verizon Center sat about 20 miles from their campus.

story.text: UConn opened 7-for-10 from the floor but could not shake the Patriots. Two free throws by Will Thomas with 3:07 left in the half put George Mason ahead 29-28, its only lead of the half. UConn answered with a 15-2 run and led 43-31 after Rashad Anderson's 3-pointer with 10 seconds left.

Folarin Campbell's three-point play in the final seconds made it 43-34 at the half. Mason pulled within one early in the second half with an 8-0 run, and Campbell's 3-pointer at 12:32 tied it at 49. Lamar Butler's 3 at 11:12 gave Mason its first lead of the half, 52-51.

The Patriots made six straight 3-pointers in the second half. From the 10:37 mark of regulation to the end of overtime, Jim Larranaga never substituted. Jai Lewis' jumper at 5:54 put Mason ahead to stay in regulation, 64-63, and Tony Skinn's 3 at 4:58 made it 67-63.

Mason kept going inside to Lewis and Thomas, even though UConn had led the nation in blocked shots five seasons running. The Patriots' three frontcourt starters outscored UConn's 54-34 and outrebounded them 21-15.

sequence.text: Marcus Williams scores on a layup, gets fouled by Butler and makes the free throw. UConn is within one.
Butler steals the ball, gets fouled by Anderson and makes both free throws. Mason by four.
Williams drives the lane and scores, then UConn calls timeout.
Skinn misses the front end of a one-and-one. Rudy Gay rebounds.
Denham Brown drives down the left side, goes under the basket and flips up a reverse layup. It bounces on the rim three times and drops through as the buzzer sounds. Overtime.
Thomas hits a jumper to open overtime. Mason scores first and never trails again.
Campbell's baseline fadeaway makes it a four-point game.
Anderson airballs a 3-pointer that would have cut the lead to one.
Brown misses a 3, but UConn keeps the ball, and Williams buries a 3-pointer. UConn is within two.
Lewis misses two free throws with 6.1 seconds left, which leaves UConn one last chance. Brown grabs the rebound.
Brown passes up a 17-footer, steps back to the left wing and shoots a 3 for the win. It hits the rim and bounces away at the buzzer. George Mason is going to the Final Four.

numbers.label: No. 1 seeds in the Final Four — a first since the field expanded to 64 teams in 1985
Mason's seed. Only one double-digit seed had reached a Final Four before: 1986 LSU, also an 11
Mason players who went the last 10:37 of regulation and all of overtime without a substitution
free throws Mason missed in the final 41 seconds of overtime, which kept UConn alive
Huskies drafted three months later, the first time any school had five players picked in a two-round draft

quotes.text: I thought we had dodged a bullet. We needed an adrenaline shot and we got it.
quotes.role: UConn coach, on Brown's tying layup

quotes.text: Now we have to beat them in a five-minute game.
quotes.role: George Mason coach, recalling what he told his team before overtime

quotes.text: They played tough and have a lot of heart.
By George, the dream is alive!
quotes.when: live call at the final buzzer

aftermath.text: George Mason went to the Final Four in Indianapolis and lost to Florida 73-58 in the national semifinals, finishing 27-8.
UConn finished 30-4. That June, Gay, Armstrong, Williams and Boone went in the first round of the NBA draft and Brown in the second.

legacy.text: Mason became the first team from the CAA to get this far, and the first true outsider in the Final Four since Penn and Indiana State in 1979.
